title: Read the cart cookie without rebuilding anything else

blocks.text: The shop keeps each visitor's cart in a cookie: the `Cart`, written with Java serialization by `CartCookie.write`. The browser sends the cookie back with every request, so its bytes are whatever the visitor, or anyone who can change their traffic, chooses to send. The shop's class path holds hundreds of `Serializable` classes from its own code and its libraries, and some of them start work when they are rebuilt.

Write `read(cookie)` in `src/main/java/practice/CartCookie.java`. A cookie that holds a cart comes back as that cart. A cookie that holds anything else, at the top or anywhere inside the cart, is refused with an `IOException`, and no code of any other class runs while it is read. Serializing a cart writes a `Cart`, the `ArrayList` of its lines, that list's `Object[]`, and each `CartLine`.

cases.says: a cookie written from a cart, with lines or empty, reads back as an equal cart
a cookie holding another Serializable class is refused before that class's readObject runs, not after
another class nested inside a real cart is refused too, before its readObject runs

origin.section: Check Classes With a Filter Before readObject Builds Them, Not the Result After

concepts: A cast or check after readObject comes after every class's own readObject has run; an ObjectInputFilter set on the stream is asked about each class, nested ones too, before it is built.
